questions.question: Which logging calls are UNSAFE in a STDIO-based MCP server because they write to stdout? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: print() in Python
console.log() in TypeScript/JavaScript
console.error() in TypeScript/JavaScript
System.out.println() in Java
fmt.Println() in Go

questions.explanation: Anything writing to stdout corrupts the JSON-RPC stream: print(), console.log(), System.out.println(), fmt.Println(). console.error() writes to stderr and is safe (as are logging libraries targeting stderr/files).

questions.question: Your server doesn't appear in Claude for Desktop after editing claude_desktop_config.json. Which checks match the official troubleshooting list? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Validate the config file's JSON syntax
Ensure the server path is absolute, not relative
Fully quit and reopen Claude Desktop (closing the window isn't enough)
Check ~/Library/Logs/Claude (mcp.log, mcp-server-NAME.log) for errors
Reinstall the operating system

questions.explanation: The documented checklist: config syntax, absolute paths, a complete restart, and reading the MCP logs. OS reinstall is not on the list.

questions.question: Which deployment paths does the build-mcp-server agent skill choose between? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Remote Streamable HTTP (default for wrapping cloud APIs)
MCP Apps (interactive widgets rendered in chat)
MCP Bundles / MCPB (local server packaged with its runtime)
Local stdio (prototyping, with an upgrade path to MCPB)
Browser extension

questions.explanation: The skill routes to one of four paths: remote Streamable HTTP, MCP apps (via build-mcp-app), MCPB (via build-mcpb), or local stdio. Browser extensions aren't a path.

questions.question: In the build-client tutorial, which statements about tool-call handling are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The client fetches tools/list and maps each tool's name, description, and input schema into the model API's tool format
A failing tool answers with is_error set rather than raising in the client
Tool results are appended to the conversation and sent back to the model for a final response
The model executes tools directly on the server without the client's involvement
CallToolResult.content is a list of typed blocks, so code narrows to text blocks before reading .text

questions.explanation: The client is always in the loop: it maps tools for the model, executes the model's requested calls through the MCP session, checks is_error, and feeds results back. The model never talks to the server directly.

questions.question: Which entries belong in a claude_desktop_config.json server definition? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: command — the executable to launch
args — arguments such as the absolute path to your server script
env — environment variables like API keys
port — the TCP port Claude should connect to
All of the above

questions.explanation: STDIO servers are subprocesses: command/args/env under the mcpServers key. There is no port — stdio doesn't use TCP, which sinks D and E.

questions.question: Which system requirements do the official quickstarts state? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Python quickstart: Python 3.10+ and MCP SDK 2.0.0+
TypeScript quickstart: Node.js 20 or higher
Client tutorial (Python): uv for project setup and an Anthropic API key in .env
Inspector: Node 22.19.0 or newer
Inspector: Node 18 or higher with npm installed

questions.explanation: All four requirements come straight from the docs — a legitimate 'All of the above'.

questions.question: Your freshly-configured stdio server crashes Claude Desktop's connection immediately. Which are plausible documented causes? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A print()/console.log() call writing to stdout and corrupting the JSON-RPC stream
A relative path in args that resolves differently for the Claude Desktop process
Invalid JSON syntax in claude_desktop_config.json
Only closing the Claude window instead of fully quitting after the config change
The server not implementing notifications/initialized handshake

questions.explanation: Every one of these is on the official troubleshooting list, making E correct too.

questions.question: Which statements about the MCP server-development agent skills are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: The mcp-server-dev plugin bundles build-mcp-server, build-mcp-app, and build-mcpb
Remote Streamable HTTP is the default path for wrapping cloud APIs
MCPB packages a local server together with its runtime for one-click install
The skills only support Python servers
All of the above

questions.explanation: The skills cover multiple languages and deployment shapes; the Python-only claim is false, so 'All of the above' fails.
